items.title: Section: A New Topic Opens — Why Exactly Four Absorptions

items.zh: 復次嗢拕南曰：數、及所對治、支分、廣建立、遠離、苦、散動、上支分、差別。問：如先所說四種靜慮，何因緣故唯四靜慮，不增不減。答：由能究竟超苦樂故。所以者何？從初靜慮乃至第四，漸超苦樂方究竟故。
items.en: Furthermore, the summary verse says: number, and what is overcome; factors, and their extensive establishment; seclusion, suffering, agitation; and the differences among the upper factors. Question: as previously stated, there are four absorptions — for what reason exactly four, neither more nor fewer? Answer: because this alone brings one completely beyond suffering and pleasure. Why is this so? Because from the first absorption through the fourth, suffering and pleasure are progressively transcended until this is complete.

items.title: Section: What Each of the Four Absorptions Actually Overcomes

items.zh: 云何名初靜慮所治？謂有五種。一者、欲貪，二、欲、恚、害三種尋思，三者、憂苦，四者、犯戒，五者、散亂。云何第二靜慮所治？亦有五種、一、初靜慮貪，二、尋伺，三、苦，四、掉，五、定下劣性。云何第三靜慮所治？謂有四種。一、第二靜慮貪，二、喜，三、踊躍，四、定下劣性。云何第四靜慮所治？謂有五種。一、入息、出息，二、第三靜慮貪，三、樂，四、於樂發悟，五、定下劣性。
items.en: What does the first absorption overcome? Five things: craving for sensual desire; the three deliberations of desire, malice, and harm; grief and suffering; transgressing precepts; and distraction. What does the second overcome? Also five: attachment to the first absorption; investigation and reflection; suffering; restlessness; and inferior quality of concentration. What does the third overcome? Four things: attachment to the second absorption; joy; exuberant agitation; and inferior quality of concentration. What does the fourth overcome? Five things: in-breath and out-breath; attachment to the third absorption; bliss; the intention seeking bliss; and inferior quality of concentration.

items.title: Section: Five Factors of the First Absorption, Four of the Second

items.zh: 問：初靜慮有幾支？答：有五支。何等為五？一、尋，二、伺，三、喜，四、樂，五、心一境性。問：第二靜慮有幾支？答：有四支。何等為四？一、內等淨，二、喜，三、樂，四、心一境性。問：內等淨何法為自性？答：念、正知、捨為自性。
items.en: Question: how many factors does the first absorption have? Answer: five. What are the five? Investigation, reflection, joy, bliss, and one-pointedness of mind. Question: how many factors does the second absorption have? Answer: four. What are the four? Inner clarity, joy, bliss, and one-pointedness of mind. Question: what is inner clarity's own nature? Answer: mindfulness, clear knowing, and equanimity are its nature.

items.title: Section: The Third Absorption's Deep Immersion, and the Fourth's Utter Stillness

items.zh: 問：第三靜慮有幾支？答：有五支。何等為五？一、念，二、正知，三、捨，四、樂，五、心一境性。問：第四靜慮有幾支？答：有四支。何等為四？一、捨清淨，二、念清淨，三、不苦不樂，四、心一境性。
items.en: Question: how many factors does the third absorption have? Answer: five. What are the five? Mindfulness, clear knowing, equanimity, bliss, and one-pointedness of mind. Question: how many factors does the fourth absorption have? Answer: four. What are the four? Purified equanimity, purified mindfulness, neither painful nor pleasant feeling, and one-pointedness of mind.

items.zh: 初靜慮中念、正知、捨，由尋伺門之所引發，是故雖有而不宣說。第二靜慮，由彼自性能有作業，又由踊躍心隨煩惱之所纏縛，是故顯示內等淨名。第三靜慮，心隨煩惱已遠離故，顯彼自相，是故說彼離喜貪故。初靜慮中離欲貪故，非離喜貪。第二靜慮離尋伺貪故，非離喜貪。第四靜慮，即彼顯示最極清淨。是故當知，一切靜慮彼皆隨轉，如其所應。

items.title: Section: Why Mindfulness and Wisdom Are Named Only Where They Are Most Needed

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，於四靜慮建立如是五支、四支？答：住所依故，住饒益故，住自性故。
items.en: Question: for what reason are five or four factors established in the four absorptions as they are? Answer: through abiding in what is depended upon, abiding in what benefits, and abiding in the absorption's own nature.

items.title: Section: Six Ways of Seeing the Same Three-Part Pattern

items.zh: 復有差別。謂思惟所緣故，受用所緣故，於緣不散故。復有差別。謂饒益所依故，增上心所依故，增上慧所依故。復有差別。謂為對治三雜染住所對治故。云何名為三雜染住所對治耶？一、染污住，二、苦惱住，三、愚癡住。復有差別。謂受欲者相似法故。諸受欲者，略有三種正所作事，能顯彼是受用欲者。一、正求財寶；二、求財寶已，能正受用；三、於彼自在，隨意所為。如是修習諸靜慮者，亦有三種正所作事，當知依彼建立支分，如其所應。復有差別。謂為對治自苦惱行，應知建立諸靜慮支。如是略有三種對治。一、對治缺減對治，二、身心逼惱對治，三、於外境界其心流散不寂靜對治。
items.en: There is a further distinction: contemplating the object, enjoying the object, and remaining undistracted towards the object. A further distinction: serving as the basis of benefit, as the basis of the higher training in mind, and as the basis of the higher training in wisdom. A further distinction: countering three kinds of defilement-bound abiding — tainted abiding, suffering abiding, and deluded abiding. A further distinction: resembling one who enjoys the objects of desire. A further distinction: countering one's own suffering, briefly of three kinds — the antidote to a deficiency of antidote, the antidote to bodily and mental distress, and the antidote to a mind scattered towards external objects and unsettled.

items.title: Section: Why the First Absorption Names Two Things It Leaves Behind

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，初靜慮中說離欲已，復說遠離惡不善法？答：為欲顯示諸欲自相故，及為顯示諸欲過患相故。過患相者，由彼諸欲發起惡行，墜墮極下惡處所故，說名為惡；違善生故，復名不善。復有差別。為欲顯示煩惱雜染斷故，及為顯示先所積集業雜染斷故。復有差別。為欲顯示諸在家者受用事門諸欲斷故，及為顯示諸出家者由尋思門諸欲斷故。復有差別。為欲顯示欲尋思斷故，及為顯示恚、害尋思斷故。復有差別。為欲顯示外道諸仙所得相故，及為顯示離彼退已行呪詛故。
items.en: Question: why, having said desire is left behind in the first absorption, does it further say evil, unwholesome states are left behind? Answer: to show desire's own mark, and to show the danger such desire produces. A further distinction: to show the severing of affliction defilement, and the severing of accumulated karma defilement. A further distinction: to show householders leaving behind desire within the domain of actual enjoyment, and renunciants leaving it behind through the gateway of deliberation. A further distinction: to show the severing of deliberation on desire, and of deliberation on malice and harm. A further distinction: to show what non-Buddhist sages likewise attain, and to show that, having fallen from it, they resort to curses.

blocks.text: Why exactly four meditations, and what each one leaves behind.
Master Cháng Bǎi: four are enough to pass fully beyond pain and pleasure: the first passes beyond grief, the second pain, the third joy, the fourth pleasure.
Master Cháng Bǎi: from the fourth on there is no in- or out-breath.
Investigation is coarse thought, reflection fine; one-pointedness binds the mind to its object. In the second, the mind need no longer investigate, and rests evenly: "inner evenness and purity".

Master Cháng Bǎi: having seen that joy stirs, one keeps attending so that joy does not arise again. The fourth is free of eight disturbances: investigation, reflection, joy, pleasure, grief, pain, out-breath, in-breath.

(Untranslated, 0649b08: mindfulness, clear knowing, and equanimity are present in the first meditation but not named there; the second is named "inner purity" because of its exuberant joy; the third is named for leaving joy; the fourth for utmost purity.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: investigation and reflection are what the first meditation relies on; joy and bliss its benefit; one-pointedness its very nature.
Master Cháng Bǎi: for householders the desire for sexual pleasure is cut; for renunciants the desire arising through thought. Anger can also make one lose concentration.
The fourth meditation is "free of eight disturbances", including breath. Each meditation is defined less by what it adds than by what it leaves behind.

quiz.q: The verse phrase is rendered "and the differences among the upper factors." Why does it miscount the topics?
options: no miscount: it is one topic among eight, as the prose and lecture both have it
the verse has ten, and two are lost
the verse has seven, and one is added
上支分 and 差別 are two topics of nine, and the English merges them, leaving eight
quiz.why: The lecture counts nine topics, with upper factors eighth and differences ninth; Master Cháng Bǎi takes agitation just before them. The English merges the last two, and the prose question on the eighth is also missing.

quiz.q: Why are there exactly four absorptions?
options: because this alone brings one completely beyond suffering and pleasure, complete by the fourth
because the three realms plus liberation make four places
because each element has its own absorption
because each noble truth has its own absorption
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: establishing four is enough to transcend pain and pleasure fully. The first passes beyond grief, the second pain, the third joy, and the fourth pleasure. So the number comes from what must be left behind.

quiz.q: The first absorption overcomes grief and suffering, and the second also suffering. How does Master Cháng Bǎi reconcile this?
options: the text errs and 苦 at the first level should be deleted, as he proposes
the first has not left the root of pain, yet treats pain arising with grief; only the second is free of the incapacity of pain
the first treats bodily pain, the second mental
the two are the same, a repetition
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though the root of pain is not yet left, pain arising with grief can be treated; the incapacity of the pain root remains, and in the second absorption pain no longer obstructs. So neither "already cut" nor "untouched" is right.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain breathing and the intention seeking bliss in the fourth absorption?
options: one lengthens the breath, and 發悟 is realising nirvana's bliss, to be sought here
breathing is distraction, treated by counting breaths
it means pleasant feeling is cut
after the fourth there is no in- or out-breath, and what is overcome is the attention to gaining bliss
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from the fourth absorption on there is no in- or out-breath; what is treated is the attention expecting to gain pleasure. The English "the intention seeking bliss" agrees with him, so 發悟 here is not an awakening.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say is the nature of inner clarity?
options: mindfulness, clear knowing, and equanimity
faith, since clear confidence arises once investigation is gone
joy and bliss
one-pointedness of mind
quiz.why: The treatise's answer differs from the Abhidharma view that takes faith as its nature. Master Cháng Bǎi: clear knowing notes at once when mindfulness lapses and returns to the practice; equanimity is a mind neither restless nor dull, upright and even.

quiz.q: 內等淨 is rendered "Inner clarity." Compared with the lecture, what is lost?
options: nothing: it means only a clear mind, with no sense of evenness, as the lecture says
內 is lost
one-pointedness is lost
等: the mind is even as well as pure, free from the stir of investigation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind need no longer make coarse or fine investigation, and can rest evenly and purely on the object directly; this is inner evenness and purity. "Clarity" catches purity only and misses evenness.

quiz.q: What are the four factors of the fourth absorption?
options: inner clarity, joy, bliss, and one-pointedness, kept from the second
mindfulness, clear knowing, equanimity, bliss
purified equanimity, purified mindfulness, neither painful nor pleasant feeling, and one-pointedness
investigation, reflection, equanimity, one-pointedness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is free of eight disturbances: investigation, reflection, joy, pleasure, grief, pain, out-breath, and in-breath, with neither the comfort of joy and pleasure nor the discomfort of grief and pain.

quiz.q: Per Master Cháng Bǎi, what are the factors of dependence and benefit in the higher absorptions?
options: mindfulness, clear knowing, and equanimity are what is relied on; neutral feeling is the fourth's benefit
investigation is always the basis and joy always the benefit, the same in all four
one-pointedness is what is depended upon
equanimity is the benefit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what is attained by relying on mindfulness, clear knowing, and equanimity makes these the factors of dependence; neutral feeling is the benefit of the fourth; and one-pointedness is the essence. This assignment follows the lecture.

quiz.q: 住自性故 is rendered "abiding in one's own nature." Why does "one's" mislead?
options: it does not: it means abiding in one's inherent buddha-nature, as the lecture says
it is the essence of the absorption itself, not the practitioner's nature
"nature" should be "lineage"
it should be "abiding in one's own lineage"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the one-pointedness factor is the very essence of the concentration, and is called abiding in its nature. The nature belongs to the absorption, not to a person, so "its own nature" would be safer than "one's own nature."

quiz.q: 對治闕減對治 is rendered "the antidote to deficiency." What cannot be seen?
options: deficiency means lack of requisites, so this treats poverty, as the lecture explains
deficiency means damaged faculties
what is deficient is the antidote itself: the desire realm lacks good investigation to treat bad thoughts
deficiency means a short life
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the deficiency is that the desire realm lacks the good investigation needed to counter thoughts of desire, malice, and harm. So the phrase means an antidote to the lack of an antidote, which the English does not show.

quiz.q: What does the treatise first say is shown by adding "evil, unwholesome states"?
options: that the root of pain is cut, and joy is left behind, as the text says
the difference of householder and renunciant
the difference of trainee and adept
desire's own mark, and the danger that desire produces
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the practitioner is made to know the danger and leave evil states. The treatise's explanation of what "evil" and "unwholesome" mean is missing in English, so only the pairing of mark and danger is tested.

quiz.q: This is rendered "householders leaving behind desire through actual conduct." What is the issue?
options: none: householders cut desire by action and renunciants by thought, as the lecture has it
受用事門 is the class of desire cut, not the means of cutting it
在家者 should be "laity who ordain"
事門 should be "way of objects"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for householders the desire of enjoying sexual matters is cut, and for renunciants the desire arising through thought. These are two kinds of desire, not two methods, though the English suggests a method.
